review: triage 117.1c: was definitional, but it states the timing legality of special actions; reclassified as legality and skipped as covered by 116.2a-1 and 116.2e-1.

triage 117.3c: was definitional, inconsistent with 117.3b (mechanical, needs_new_fields) and 116.3; reclassified as mechanical and added scenario 117.3c-1 (holding priority to stack two Shocks under Giant Growth versus passing first).
117.3b-1 mana-ability: delta had B tap Mountain in A's main phase although B never had priority in the base; changed it to A tapping Mountain instead of casting Shock, A keeping priority.

skipped.reason: covered by 116.2a-1 (playing a land only in a main phase with an empty stack) and 116.2e-1 (a special action taken whenever the player could cast an instant), the rule 116 scenarios this rule cross-references

scenarios.title: A noninstant spell is castable only in a main phase with an empty stack

setup.notes: A has priority with an empty stack. B's tapped Mountain only matters for the stack-not-empty variant.

decisions: A has priority and checks whether Grizzly Bears can be cast; if legal, A casts it tapping both Forests, then both players pass and it resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is castable (can_play true); it resolves and enters A's battlefield.

variants.label: stack-not-empty
variants.delta: B's Shock targeting A, paid with B's Mountain, is already on the stack (set up on the stack) and A has priority in response.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is not castable (can_play false) while the stack is non-empty.

variants.label: combat-step
variants.delta: The step is beginning_of_combat instead of main1 (empty stack, A has priority).
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is not castable (can_play false) outside a main phase.

scenarios.forge_notes: The stack-not-empty variant puts B's Shock on the stack through setup.stack: {card Shock, controller B, targets [A]}.

scenarios.title: An instant is castable whenever the player has priority, including with a non-empty stack

setup.notes: A has priority in the beginning of combat step with an empty stack.

decisions: A has priority and checks whether Shock can be cast; if legal, A casts Shock targeting B, tapping Mountain, then both players pass and it resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Shock is castable (can_play true); it resolves and B's life is 18.

variants.label: stack-not-empty
variants.delta: A passes priority; B casts Shock targeting A, tapping Mountain; A receives priority with B's Shock on the stack.
variants.expected: Shock is still castable by A (can_play true) with a spell on the stack; A's Shock resolves first and B's life is 18, then B's Shock resolves and A's life is 18.

variants.label: no-priority
variants.delta: The step is untap instead of beginning_of_combat.
variants.expected: Shock is not castable (can_play false) because no player receives priority in the untap step.

scenarios.forge_notes: The untap-step variant may not be reachable through a puzzle state; it can be checked by asking the playability query before priority is granted.

scenarios.title: An activated ability is activatable whenever its controller has priority

setup.notes: Mogg Fanatic has been on the battlefield since an earlier turn. A has priority with an empty stack. B's tapped Mountain only matters for the stack-not-empty variant.

decisions: A has priority and checks whether Mogg Fanatic's ability can be activated; if legal, A activates it, sacrificing Mogg Fanatic, targeting B.
Both players pass; the ability resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: The ability is activatable (can_play true); Mogg Fanatic goes to A's graveyard as a cost and B's life is 19.

variants.label: stack-not-empty
variants.delta: B's Shock targeting Mogg Fanatic, paid with B's Mountain, is already on the stack (set up on the stack) and A has priority.
variants.expected: The ability is still activatable with a spell on the stack; A sacrifices Mogg Fanatic in response targeting B, the ability resolves first (B's life is 19) and B's Shock then fizzles.

variants.label: no-priority
variants.delta: The step is untap instead of beginning_of_combat.
variants.expected: The ability is not activatable (can_play false) because no player receives priority in the untap step.

scenarios.forge_notes: The stack-not-empty variant puts B's Shock on the stack through setup.stack: {card Shock, controller B, targets [Mogg Fanatic]}.

scenarios.title: A mana ability can be activated while paying a cost during resolution, when no player has priority

setup.notes: A casts Grizzly Bears with two Forests; B responds with Force Spike. A's third Forest is untapped.

decisions: A casts Grizzly Bears, tapping two Forests.
B casts Force Spike targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Island.
Both players pass; Force Spike resolves and A is asked to pay {1}; A pays by tapping the third Forest for mana during the resolution.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: A's Forest mana ability is activatable during the resolution of Force Spike; A pays {1}, Force Spike does nothing, and after both players pass Grizzly Bears resolves onto A's battlefield.

variants.label: no-source
variants.delta: A controls only two Forests, not three.
variants.expected: A has no mana ability to activate; the payment cannot be made and Force Spike counters Grizzly Bears, which goes to A's graveyard.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge asks the spell's controller to pay the UnlessCost on resolution; the scripted decision must be the payment.

scenarios.title: A cast trigger triggers during casting and goes on the stack above the spell

setup.notes: A has priority with an empty stack.

decisions: A casts Shock targeting B's Grizzly Bears, tapping Mountain.
Guttersnipe triggers during casting; before A receives priority again, its trigger is put on the stack above Shock.
Both players pass; the trigger resolves, then both pass again and Shock resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Guttersnipe's trigger fires; it is put on the stack above Shock only when A would receive priority, resolves first (B's life is 18 while Shock is still on the stack), then Shock resolves and B's Grizzly Bears moves to B's graveyard.

variants.label: creature-spell
variants.delta: A casts Grizzly Bears (tapping Forest and Mountain) instead of Shock.
variants.expected: Guttersnipe's trigger does not fire; the stack holds only Grizzly Bears and B's life stays 20.

scenarios.title: An enters trigger that triggers during resolution goes on the stack only when a player would next receive priority

setup.notes: A has priority with an empty stack.

decisions: A casts Grizzly Bears, tapping both Forests; both players pass and it resolves.
Soul Warden triggers during the resolution; it is put on the stack when A would receive priority, then both players pass and the trigger resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Soul Warden's trigger fires when Grizzly Bears enters; after Grizzly Bears resolves the trigger sits on the stack with A's life still 20, then resolves and A's life is 21.

variants.label: noncreature-spell
variants.delta: A casts Shock targeting B (tapping Mountain) instead of Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: No creature enters, so Soul Warden's trigger does not fire; A's life stays 20 and B's life is 18.

scenarios.title: The active player receives priority at the start of a step after beginning-of-step triggers are put on the stack, but not in the untap step

setup.notes: The step begins; A has not yet received priority.

decisions: Ajani's Mantra triggers at the beginning of the upkeep and is put on the stack before A receives priority.
A receives priority with the trigger on the stack and passes; B passes; the trigger resolves and A chooses to gain 1 life.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: The trigger is on the stack when A first receives priority in the upkeep; it resolves and A's life is 21.

variants.label: untap
variants.delta: The step is untap instead of upkeep.
variants.expected: No player receives priority in the untap step; nothing is on the stack and A's life stays 20.

variants.label: draw
variants.delta: The step is draw instead of upkeep.
variants.expected: A draws Grizzly Bears as a turn-based action before receiving priority; Grizzly Bears is in A's hand when A first has priority, the upkeep trigger does not fire and A's life stays 20.

scenarios.title: The active player receives priority after a spell resolves, even if the nonactive player cast it

setup.notes: A has priority with an empty stack and holds Shock; B holds Shock.

decisions: A casts Shock targeting B, tapping Mountain; both players pass and Shock resolves.
After resolution A receives priority and casts nothing.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: B's life is 18; the caster A, who is also the active player, receives priority after Shock resolves.

variants.label: nonactive-caster
variants.delta: A passes priority with an empty stack, then B casts Shock targeting A, tapping Mountain; both pass and it resolves.
variants.expected: A's life is 18; A, the active player, receives priority after B's Shock resolves, before B does.

variants.label: mana-ability
variants.delta: A taps Mountain for mana instead of casting Shock; nothing is put on the stack.
variants.expected: No spell or ability resolves; A, who activated the mana ability, still holds priority and B's life stays 20.

scenarios.forge_notes: Priority holder after resolution is a checked outcome only if the harness exposes it; otherwise assert who may act first.

scenarios.title: A player who casts a spell receives priority afterward and can cast another before the opponent responds

setup.notes: A has priority with an empty stack.

decisions: A casts the first Shock targeting B's Grizzly Bears, tapping a Mountain.
A receives priority and casts the second Shock targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping the other Mountain.
B receives priority for the first time with both Shocks on the stack and casts Giant Growth targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Forest.
Players pass in succession after each resolution until the stack is empty.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Stack bottom to top: Shock, Shock, Giant Growth. Giant Growth resolves first (Grizzly Bears 5/5), then both Shocks resolve; Grizzly Bears survives with 4 damage marked.

variants.label: passes-first
variants.delta: A passes priority after casting the first Shock instead of casting the second; A casts the second Shock when A next receives priority, after B's Giant Growth.
variants.expected: Stack bottom to top: Shock, Giant Growth, Shock. The second Shock resolves first and Grizzly Bears (2/2) moves to B's graveyard; Giant Growth and the first Shock fizzle.

scenarios.forge_notes: No does_not_fire variant: every cast by a player with priority gives that player priority again, so the rule has no branch where it applies and its effect fails. Which player holds priority is not a record field; the stack order is the observable consequence.

scenarios.title: The top stack object resolves only when all players pass in succession; otherwise it stays on the stack

setup.notes: A has priority with an empty stack.

decisions: A casts Shock targeting B's Grizzly Bears, tapping Mountain.
A passes priority; B passes priority; Shock resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Both players passed in succession: Shock resolves and Grizzly Bears moves to B's graveyard.

variants.label: response
variants.delta: After A passes, B casts Giant Growth targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Forest, instead of passing; A then passes and B passes.
variants.expected: B's action interrupted the succession, so Shock stayed on the stack; Giant Growth resolves first (Grizzly Bears 5/5), then after another full round of passes Shock resolves and Grizzly Bears survives with 2 damage marked.

variants.label: empty-stack
variants.delta: A casts no spell; A passes and B passes.
variants.expected: The stack is empty, so no object resolves and the main phase ends: the game moves to beginning_of_combat; Grizzly Bears is untouched.

scenarios.title: State-based actions repeat before triggers are put on the stack and before a player receives priority

setup.notes: Rancor is owned by B and enchants B's Grizzly Bears (4/2 with trample).

decisions: A casts Shock targeting B's Grizzly Bears, tapping Mountain.
Both players pass; Shock resolves, then the state-based check runs before anyone receives priority.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: In the first check Grizzly Bears (damage 2, toughness 2) dies; in the repeated check Rancor, no longer attached, goes to B's graveyard; only then Rancor's return trigger is put on the stack, before A receives priority.

variants.label: survives
variants.delta: B's creature is Centaur Courser (3/3, so 5/3 with Rancor) instead of Grizzly Bears, and Rancor is attached to it.
variants.expected: Centaur Courser survives with 2 damage marked, no state-based action is performed and Rancor stays attached; no trigger is put on the stack.

scenarios.forge_notes: Rancor's trigger fires once Rancor is in the graveyard from the battlefield; its return to hand happens when that trigger resolves.

scenarios.title: A spell cast in response to another resolves first

setup.notes: A has priority with an empty stack.

decisions: A casts Shock targeting B's Grizzly Bears, tapping Mountain.
B responds with Giant Growth targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Forest.
Both players pass; Giant Growth resolves, then both pass again and Shock resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Giant Growth, cast in response, resolves first: Grizzly Bears is 5/5 when Shock resolves and survives with 2 damage marked.

variants.label: no-response
variants.expected: Shock resolves with no spell above it and Grizzly Bears (2/2) moves to B's graveyard.

variants.label: counter-response
variants.delta: After B's Giant Growth, A casts the second Shock targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping the second Mountain.
variants.expected: The second Shock, cast last, resolves first: Grizzly Bears (2/2) dies; Giant Growth and the first Shock fizzle because their target is gone.
